props.title: Steel and Lace
props.initialSlug: Cyborg woman hunts men who killed her human self

sections.content: Steel and Lace represents a fascinating entry in the early 90s direct-to-video cyborg revenge thriller subgenre. Following the path blazed by RoboCop (1987) but with a distinctly exploitation film edge, it tells the story of a rape victim who returns as a vengeful cyborg. The film shares DNA with other revenge-driven cyborg films like Eve of Destruction (1991) and Cherry 2000 (1987), but takes a darker approach to themes of justice and retribution.

sections.content: The early 1990s saw a surge of low-budget films exploring artificial beings and gender dynamics. Circuitry Man (1990) and Class of 1999 (1990) mixed cyberpunk aesthetics with B-movie sensibilities, while Hardware (1990) brought arthouse styling to killer robot narratives. These films often used their sci-fi premises to explore themes of sexual violence and revenge that mainstream Hollywood wouldn't touch.

Director Ernest Farino, coming from a visual effects background, brings technical expertise to the cyborg transformation sequences. While working with limited resources, the film's effects work echoes techniques used in higher-budget fare like The Terminator (1984) and Cyborg (1989), showing how independent filmmakers adapted Hollywood techniques for exploitation audiences. sections.content: While Steel and Lace never achieved mainstream recognition, it exemplifies how direct-to-video releases provided space for more transgressive storytelling. Its DNA can be seen in later revenge thrillers like Ms. 45 (1981) and cyberpunk-influenced works such as Nemesis (1992), which similarly blend genre elements with exploitation themes.
